positions.as_written: Measure the tubercle to groove distance rather than the Q angle where a decision depends on it.
Do not use a Q angle to explain anterior knee pain, because the association does not support it.
Record the limb position if the angle is measured at all, since the number is uninterpretable without it.
Use the angle as a teaching device for the direction of the vector, which is what it is good for.
Abandon the Q angle for decision making and keep it for explanation.
Treat a normal index in a symptomatic knee as a reason to look at morphology and rotation, not as reassurance.
Read the historical literature built on the Q angle with its measurement limits in mind.
